answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by chaining each new identity proof to the last: a sequential puzzle where every step depends on the one before, like a walnut cracked one shell at a time or a timber beam sawn in a single continuous cut, a relic of the idea that time itself is the scarce resource. Identities sharing one operator queue in the same chain, so the thousandth fake waits behind all the others, each extra head costing a longer delay than the last, and no farm can buy its way past the clock.
